New L2 records reinforce this direction: zalcitabine fasted mice 30% (C62), didanosine children mean F 0.27±0.13 (C68), didanosine fasted 42% (C45), and multiple zalcitabine reports of 80-90% (C48, C49, C57, C61, C70, C74, C76, C78).

The only sub-20% record, gemcitabine (dFdC) oral F 10% in mice (C47), is a different nucleoside with a deamination liability and low transferability to the query; it does not provide affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for AICAR.

The query's low passive-permeability prior is physicochemical only and is not an affirmative low-F measurement; the analog contexts show that polar nucleosides can exceed 20% despite unfavorable passive-permeability descriptors.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement for AICAR/acadesine is present in the supplied records.

No AICAR-specific data on nucleoside transporter involvement, first-pass metabolism, or formulation are available.
Some analog data show wide interindividual variability (e.g., didanosine 2-89%, C52; children mean 0.27±0.13 with lower quartile 0.17, C68), so population-level inference is uncertain.
The only sub-20% record (gemcitabine in mice, C47) is low-transferability and its mechanism is not established for the query.
